content.value: The field-weighted relevance function the Indx Engine ranks with — title outranks body, computed natively rather than borrowed from Postgres.

BM25F is the field-aware variant of BM25. Where plain BM25 scores a document as one bag of words, BM25F splits it into fields and weights each one before combining — in Barkpark that means a title match counts for more than a body match. The Indx Engine uses BM25F as its core ranking signal across the Document corpus.
Postgres Search reaches a similar "title beats body" outcome by a different mechanism: it runs
over the Search Vector, whose weight classes (
for body) are baked in at index time via
. BM25F applies its field weights at query time, so they can be tuned without rebuilding an index — Postgres bakes them into a generated column that only a Migration can recompute.

Both engines sit behind the one Search contract and return identical Search Facets. They also share the upstream Auto Correction Loop and Synonyms expansion, so a learned correction reaches BM25F and

alike. Which engine wins on a given query mix is settled empirically by the Golden Eval harness — and the clickstream in Search Intelligence is where a future re-rank of these field weights would draw its training signal.
